learning_outcomes.text: To apply in theoretical developments and simple applications the law and the properties of ideal gases based in particular on the developments of the kinetic theory of gases.
To define and apply within the framework of simple exercises pertaining to open and closed systems the first principle of thermodynamics for systems of constant composition.

Mathematically define and apply the concept of entropy in connection with heat exchange. In particular, the student will be able to expose and use the consequences of the existence of entropy for cycles.

To apply the principles of thermodynamics to systems whose composition is variable (chemical reactions) based on the notions of chemical potential, chemical equilibrium and standard enthalpy of reaction.
To describe and calculate the state of an oxidation-reduction reaction in an electrochemical cell as well as the impact of a change in parameters (concentrations, etc.) on the electromotive force.
To explain the concept of speed and order of a global chemical reaction or extracted from a reaction mechanism.
To link kinetics and equilibrium for elementary reactions.
Base of scientific and technical knowledge.
Documenting and summarizing the state of current knowledge in the field considered.
Collectively commit to a work plan, a timetable and the roles to be played.
Make a convincing presentation using modern communication techniques.

syllabus_topics: ideal gases and kinetic theory of gases
complements on the first principle of thermodynamics and application to thermal cycles
second principle of thermodynamics applied to thermal cycles

assessment_methods.method: Final written examination: open-ended questions in chemistry
Final written examination: open-ended questions in thermodynamics

assessment_rules: Students are assessed individually and in writing. The final exam grade is a weighted average of the grades obtained in the various parts. Depending on the length of the exam, the weighting is 1/3, 1/3, 1/3 (4-hour exam) or 0.375, 0.375, 0.25 (3-hour exam). For the January session, a mid-term examination may count for one third of the final mark, provided the result is higher than the mark of the final examination alone. If the average of the marks obtained is between 9.01 and 9.99 out of 20, the mark is rounded up to 9. Active participation in the compulsory laboratories is assessed and included in the mark for the 'chemistry' part of the exam; this activity cannot be rescheduled in the second session and the grade obtained in January is final. For the August/September session, the mid-term test is not taken into account.
degree: Bachelor in Engineering (Bachelier en sciences de l'ingénieur, orientation ingénieur civil) - FSA1BA
